mainTopic: How a single young goat could produce enough offspring within its first year to be obligated in מעשר בהמה, and what exactly the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון disagree about
overview: This amud continues a ברייתא that counts how many offspring a young goat (גדיה) and its offspring can produce within one year, enough to be obligated in מעשר בהמה. First the גמרא suggests that the ברייתא's count shows the תנא holds that a מטנפת (an animal that expelled a murky discharge) cannot give birth again within its year. It then rejects this: the ברייתא deals with animals that really gave birth, and a real birth is different from a discharge. Next the גמרא quotes רבי שמעון, 'I saw a goat…', and asks what practical difference there is between him and the תנא קמא. It offers several possible answers, each one granting more shared ground. (1) They argue about זעירי's rule that a discharge counts only if it prevents pregnancy for 30 days. (2) Everyone accepts זעירי, but they argue whether an animal can give birth after incomplete months (למקוטעין). (3) Everyone also rejects early birth, and they argue whether part of a day counts as a whole day (מקצת היום ככולו). (4) Everyone accepts מקצת היום ככולו, and they argue whether a מחוסר זמן (an animal too young for the מזבח) enters the pen to be tithed.

steps.title: Does the ברייתא hold that a discharging animal cannot give birth again within its year?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the way the ברייתא counts the offspring shows that the תנא holds a מטנפת cannot return and give birth within its first year.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say the תנא holds that an animal that expelled a murky discharge does not return and give birth within its year?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a suggestion: from the way the ברייתא counts the births, maybe its author holds a specific rule about a מטנפת. This is a proposal that the next step will test.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's count of births in one year leaves no room for a second birth from the same animal. The גמרא wonders whether this means the תנא believes that even an animal that only expelled a murky discharge (not a real baby) cannot give birth again that same year.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say — introduces a suggested inference

An animal that expelled a murky discharge (instead of a live baby)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues analysis of the ברייתא about a goat's offspring within its year (on the previous amud).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the ברייתא's count implies that a מטנפת cannot give birth again within its year.

steps.title: No proof: a real birth is different from a discharge
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion: even if a מטנפת can give birth again within its year, an animal that actually gave birth certainly cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if you say that a discharging animal does return and give birth within its year, an animal that truly gave birth certainly does not return and give birth within its year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the suggestion from step 1. The ברייתא is talking about animals that really gave birth, so it tells us nothing about a מטנפת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A discharge is a weaker event than a real birth, so a מטנפת might recover quickly. But a יולדת, an animal that actually gave birth, surely needs more time. So the ברייתא's count fits even the view that a מטנפת can give birth again.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you were to say — 'even granting the other side'
An animal that actually gave birth
Certainly

phrases.english: If you were to say:
a discharging animal returns and gives birth within its year —
an animal that gave birth certainly does not return

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference proposed in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof is rejected entirely; the ברייתא does not show any view about a מטנפת.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The suggestion ignored the difference between a discharge and a real birth; the ברייתא only deals with real births.

steps.title: What is the difference between the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון's line 'I saw a goat…' and asks what practical difference there is between him and the תנא קמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: I saw a goat (that became obligated in מעשר within its year), etc. What difference is there between the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new piece of the ברייתא, quoting רבי שמעון, and asks how his view really differs from the first opinion. This sets up the answers in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון stresses that this happened 'within its year,' while the תנא קמא does not say that. The גמרא wants to know what real case would come out differently between them.

keyTerms.meaning: A young female goat

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אִיכָּא בֵּין תַּנָּא קַמָּא לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: moves from the counting of the תנא קמא to רבי שמעון's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical case in which the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון would rule differently.

steps.title: First answer: they argue about the rule of זעירי
steps.stepSummary: The difference is the rule of זעירי: the תנא קמא accepts it and רבי שמעון does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is the rule of זעירי. The תנא קמא accepts זעירי's rule, and רבי שמעון does not accept זעירי's rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer: the argument depends on זעירי's rule that a discharge only counts if it keeps the animal from becoming pregnant for 30 days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picture the second-generation goats having a discharge on the first day of their seventh month. If זעירי is right, they cannot get pregnant for 30 days, so they cannot give birth before the new year starts — that is the תנא קמא. רבי שמעון does not accept זעירי, so they can get pregnant sooner and give birth within the first year.

keyTerms.meaning: There is (a difference) between them
An אמורא whose rule is that a discharge counts only if it prevents pregnancy for 30 days
He holds / accepts
He does not hold / accept

phrases.english: There is between them the rule of Ze'eiri.
The first tanna accepts Ze'eiri's rule,
and Rabbi Shimon does not accept Ze'eiri's rule.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תנא קמא accepts זעירי's 30-day rule, so the birth falls after the year; רבי שמעון rejects it, so the birth can fall within the year.

steps.title: Second answer: they argue whether an animal can give birth after incomplete months
steps.stepSummary: Alternatively, everyone accepts זעירי, and the argument is whether an animal can give birth למקוטעין (before its months are complete).
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: everyone accepts זעירי's rule, and here they argue about whether an animal gives birth after incomplete months. According to the תנא קמא, it does not give birth after incomplete months; according to רבי שמעון, it does.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a different answer: both sides agree with זעירי, but they disagree about whether a pregnancy can end a bit early.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even with זעירי's 30-day wait, if an animal can give birth before its full months are done, the birth could still fall in the first year — that is רבי שמעון. The תנא קמא holds the pregnancy must be complete, so the birth falls only in the second year.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say — introduces an alternative answer
Everyone agrees
After incomplete (shortened) months of pregnancy

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
everyone accepts Ze'eiri's rule,
and here they disagree about giving birth after incomplete months.
According to the first tanna, it does not give birth after incomplete months;
according to Rabbi Shimon, it does give birth (after incomplete months).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִית לְהוּ דִּזְעֵירִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to step 3 that keeps זעירי's rule for both sides.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both accept זעירי; the argument is whether birth can happen after incomplete months (תנא קמא: no; רבי שמעון: yes).

steps.title: Third answer: they argue whether part of a day counts as a whole day
steps.stepSummary: Alternatively, everyone agrees there is no birth למקוטעין, and the argument is about מקצת היום ככולו.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: everyone agrees that an animal does not give birth after incomplete months, and here they argue about whether part of the day counts as the whole day. According to the תנא קמא, we do not say part of the day is like the whole day; according to רבי שמעון, we do say part of the day is like the whole day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third answer: both sides accept זעירי and both reject early birth, and the whole argument comes down to a single day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If part of a day counts as a full day, the last day of the pregnancy can be counted as finished on that same day, so the birth lands on the last day of the first year — that is רבי שמעון. The תנא קמא does not count part of a day as a whole, so the earliest birth is on the first day of the second year.

keyTerms.meaning: Part of the day is considered like the whole day
We say (apply this rule)
We do not say (apply this rule)

steps.whatToRemember: So far there are three ways to explain the argument between the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון: (1) whether we accept זעירי's 30-day rule; (2) whether an animal can give birth after incomplete months; (3) whether מקצת היום ככולו. In each of these, רבי שמעון's view lets the birth fall within the first year, and the תנא קמא's view pushes it into the second year. The next step adds a fourth explanation.
steps.confusionAlert: Each 'ואיבעית אימא' does not cancel the previous answer as wrong; it offers another possible way to explain the same argument. Notice that each answer agrees to more and more shared ground, narrowing the argument to something smaller.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say,
everyone agrees it does not give birth after incomplete months,
and here they disagree about whether part of the day is like all of it:
According to the first tanna — we do not say
part of the day is like all of it;
according to Rabbi Shimon — we do say
part of the day is like all of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אֵינָהּ יוֹלֶדֶת לִמְקוּטָּעִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a third answer that keeps both זעירי's rule and the rejection of early birth, narrowing the argument further.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both accept זעירי and reject early birth; the argument is whether מקצת היום ככולו (תנא קמא: no; רבי שמעון: yes).

steps.title: The argument is about a too-young animal entering the tithing pen
steps.stepSummary: Another answer: everyone accepts מקצת היום ככולו. The real argument is whether a מחוסר זמן enters the pen for מעשר בהמה. The תנא קמא says no, and רבי שמעון says yes.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say this: everyone agrees that part of a day counts like a whole day. Here they argue about an animal that is still מחוסר זמן (too young). Does it enter the pen to be tithed or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a fourth possible explanation of the argument between the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון. It moves the argument away from מקצת היום ככולו and onto a new question about tithing very young animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6 the argument was about whether part of a day counts as a whole day. Now both sides agree that it does, so a new difference is needed. According to the Sefaria explanation, the תנא קמא holds that a מחוסר זמן (under 7 days old, not yet fit for the מזבח) does not enter the pen to be tithed. רבי שמעון holds that it does.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you want, say…' — introduces another possible answer

steps.whatToRemember: There are now four explanations of the dispute: (1) זעירי's rule, (2) birth למקוטעין, (3) מקצת היום ככולו, and (4) whether a מחוסר זמן enters the pen for מעשר.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two time questions. מקצת היום ככולו is about counting days, and here everyone agrees with it. מחוסר זמן is about whether a too-young animal can be counted for tithing, and that is the new point of argument.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the same disagreement between two תנאים can be explained in several ways. Each explanation points to a different underlying halachic issue, and here the issue is the laws of מעשר בהמה.
